name: Cinematic world
source: A product told inside one generated world: a few Codex plates of a place (an anchor image, a character or object sheet) animated as depth parallax, slow dollies, light shifts and particles, cut like a trailer with big titles and a score. Described from the atlas cinematic AI-world entry; no images are carried.

frame_device.what: Letterboxed 2.39:1 or full-frame plates of one world with a consistent light and grade, a soft vignette, film grain and a title lockup that returns.
frame_device.moves: A slow dolly or crane over the plates in 2.5D; the camera pushes in on the hero element for each idea; light and fog drift; the title cards arrive on the score's hits.

ground_motion: Depth parallax between 3 to 5 plate layers, drifting fog or particles and a breathing grade keep the world alive; the camera never stops between hits.

type.classes: A wide-tracked light serif or a clean caps sans for trailer titles; one small support face for credits and qualifiers.
type.behaviour: Titles fade and track out slowly on hits; one idea per card, 2 to 5 words; the claim card is large and held 1.5 s.

image.treatment: 3 to 6 Codex plates sharing one world bible (anchor image, style line), split into layers with depth, graded and grained; product UI is composited as a real screen plate inside the world (a holographic panel, a monolith, a window).
image.behaviour: Each plate is used 3 or more times (crops, dolly directions, grade shifts); no still holds for more than 1.2 s; every move has an ease and a purpose.

transitions: dolly through a gap into the next plate
light flare or bloom wipe on a hit
match cut on a shape between plates
dip to black on the downbeat

techniques.name: Depth dolly
techniques.what: A plate is pulled apart in depth and the camera pushes through the layers.
techniques.route: RasanCamera on 2.5D layers (cut-out plates with depth) with z-offset scale and drift; 4 to 6 s power1.inOut.

techniques.name: Hero push-in
techniques.what: The camera pushes in on the hero element for the key idea.
techniques.route: Scale 1 to 1.35 and a 3 percent drift toward the focus over 3 s; rack the focus with RasanOptics where a blur is allowed.

techniques.name: Light shift
techniques.what: The world's light changes with the story (dawn to night, cool to warm).
techniques.route: Animate a gradient-map or colour-overlay layer through 2 to 3 held grades; 1.5 s power2.inOut.

techniques.name: Particle drift
techniques.what: Dust, embers or snow drift through the frame to give air.
techniques.route: RasanOrbs or a seeded canvas particle field, parallax per layer, never random.

techniques.name: Title hit
techniques.what: A trailer title lands on the score's hit and tracks out.
techniques.route: Letter-spacing 0.4em to 0.55em over 2.5 s power1.out with a 0.3 s fade-in; hit time snapped to the music grid.

techniques.name: Screen in world
techniques.what: The real product UI is a lit surface inside the world.
techniques.route: A UI plate in a perspective plane with a rim glow only on the one control; the camera pushes into it for the proof beat.

techniques.name: Match cut on a shape
techniques.what: A circle in one plate becomes the sun or a lens in the next.
techniques.route: Place matching shape in both plates at the same screen position and scale at the cut; 0.4 s dolly through it.

techniques.name: Dip to black
techniques.what: The film dips to black on a downbeat and returns in a new place.
techniques.route: Black layer opacity 0 to 1 in 0.25 s, hold 0.2 s, back in 0.5 s; the music drops out for the hold.

techniques.name: Word choreography
techniques.what: Each word of a line enters from its own place and settles into the line with a lift; the key word last with a little more overshoot.
techniques.route: Titles are split into words and each word fades in with a 20 px drift, 0.8 s power2.out, stagger 0.2 s, tracking easing out; the key word lands last on the hit.

signature: The camera pushes through the last plate into black, and the title card with the product's name holds for two beats.

density.note: A new plate, move or title every 1.6 to 3 s; layers at the peak: 5 to 8 (back plate, mid, hero, fog, particles, grade, grain, title).

palette.note: The world bible sets the grade; a brand colour is the title tint and the screen plate's glow.

do: Share one world bible across every plate
Keep the camera moving with an ease and a purpose
Use each plate 3 or more times
Put the real UI inside the world as a lit surface
dont: Do not hold a still for more than 1.2 s
Do not mix art styles between plates
Do not generate readable UI text; typeset it
Do not stack effects on every layer
